clue.text: Put bracelets on both arms

parts.note: bracelets is old slang for the metal rings police lock round a suspect's wrists, so this is an arrest, not jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone loading jewellery onto each wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets is criminal slang for manacles, so putting them on both wrists means restraining a prisoner.

clue.text: Escape from the giraffe's enclosure

indicators.note: the words the giraffe's enclose the answer, like an animal pen at the zoo

explanation.surface: An animal breaks out of its zoo pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hegira is Muhammad's flight from Mecca to Medina in 622.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hegira was the Prophet's flight from Mecca, so any flight to safety.

clue.text: That's £50 invested in Japanese play — an ornamental work

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so these letters sit within the drama

parts.note: No (Noh) is classical Japanese masked drama
that is gives i.e., id est
the pound sign is L (libra) and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fifty pounds put into a Japanese stage show, a decorative production.
explanation.walkthrough: '£50' gives two letters: L for the pound sign and L for Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to decorate engraved silver, a kind of ornamental craft.

clue.text: Flower that makes a sweet bunch

parts.note: a sweet is candy
a tuft is a bunch of hair, grass or feathers

explanation.surface: A bloom that forms a pretty bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Candytuft is a garden plant of the genus Iberis with white or purple blooms.

clue.text: Frank is turning, using neutral

parts.note: frank means free and open
turning means wheeling, going round

explanation.surface: An outspoken person is changing direction while staying impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neutral' looks like impartial but is the gear: coasting in neutral with no drive engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Coasting in neutral, with the drive disengaged, is moving without power.

clue.text: Break off communications, having an emotional problem

definitions.meaning: end a telephone call by replacing the receiver
a psychological block or fixation that troubles someone

explanation.surface: Someone stops talking to others because of a psychological difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a phone call is to replace the receiver; as a noun the phrase means a neurosis or fixation.

clue.text: I love old Roman city intrigue

parts.note: amo is Latin, the language of old Rome, for I love
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Someone confesses affection for scheming in an ancient Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' goes with 'Roman' to mean Latin, though it seems to go with 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a secret love affair, an intrigue.

clue.text: Hand over bride with, free, present

definitions.meaning: to formally present a bride to her husband at a wedding
describing something handed out at no cost
a gift handed out to customers

explanation.surface: A father gives away his daughter at the wedding, along with a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means formally passing a bride to her husband; as a noun or adjective, a free gift.

clue.text: Area kept free for bird from Africa

indicators.note: free means released, so the letters of area kept are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Land is reserved for a native African species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like part of the reserve but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose-ringed species of small long-tailed parrot is native to Africa.

clue.text: Where to get a neat fisherman's sweater

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, and this Channel Island gives its name to a breed of dairy cow
a thick knitted woollen jersey traditionally worn by seamen

explanation.surface: Advice on where to buy a smart knitted jumper for an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective (tidy) but is the archaic noun for an ox or cow; GUERNSEY is one of the Channel Islands, home of a cattle breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Island breeds a famous dairy cow, and its name is also used for a thick knitted jersey worn by seamen.

clue.text: You could be lovers!

indicators.note: the letters of the word lovers could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A flirtatious suggestion that two people might become a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is the person doing this crossword, the definition; 'could be' signals rearranging LOVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The person working on the crossword is a puzzler who works out answers.

clue.text: Habit you can't get out of, that's the difficulty with a reefer

definitions.text: Habit you can't get out of

parts.note: straits, a strait, means a difficult situation
a reefer is a short double-breasted jacket

explanation.surface: Someone describes a drug habit, a reefer being a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reefer' suggests a cannabis cigarette but is a sailor's jacket; 'Habit' is a garment, as a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A restraining garment with long sleeves tied behind is clothing the wearer cannot escape.

clue.text: Everybody's in line for assembly.

indicators.note: everybody is placed within the abbreviation for line

parts.note: RY, short for railway, a line
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Everyone is queueing up to attend a school gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' is a railway line, abbreviated RY, not a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass meeting of supporters is a gathering or assembly.

clue.text: Impression on paper of the sea here at its height:

definitions.meaning: a faint design pressed into paper during manufacture, visible against the light

definitions.text: of the sea here at its height
definitions.meaning: the line left on a shore or structure showing how high the tide reached

explanation.surface: A drawing on paper showing the ocean at high tide.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint maker's design seen in paper held to the light; also a line marking the highest level reached by tide or flood.

clue.text: Pension off the splendid woman you called a goddess?

parts.note: splendid means super
Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: called means spoken aloud, so the word you is heard as a single letter

parts.note: the word you, said aloud
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone retires a wonderful lady they once compared to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link. 'called' signals that YOU sounds like the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire someone on a pension, especially because of age, is to make them retire.

clue.text: Gas lights now standardised?

parts.note: suggests modern lighting tubes filled with an inert gas that glows red, now commonplace

explanation.surface: A question about whether street gas lamps have become uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas lights' suggests old coal-gas lamps, but these are tubes lit by an inert gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubes filled with an inert gas that glows when electrified light signs and shopfronts.

clue.text: Church in Crimea could be very cold, of course

indicators.note: the church sits inside the rearranged letters
the letters of Crimea could be rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church on the Black Sea peninsula might be freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the place name; 'in' puts the church inside. 'of course' points to a course of a meal, a dessert, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert is a very cold course in a meal.

clue.text: Fruit dish in this order is perfect

definitions.meaning: a baked pastry filled with cooked fruit
in this kind of order means perfectly neat and tidy

explanation.surface: A dessert served in the proper sequence is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'in apple-pie order' means everything perfectly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked dessert of pastry and fruit; and the idiom meaning neat and perfectly arranged.

clue.text: Summing up, without a prior note, a submission

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the note is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: summing up means recapitulation, a restatement of the main points
re is a note of the sol-fa scale, here the one that comes first

explanation.surface: In concluding an argument, someone yields a point without a preliminary memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' says the note RE is at the front of RECAPITULATION, so removing it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender, yielding to an opponent, is an act of submission.

clue.text: It is usually spotted in a hooded cloak

definitions.meaning: a gaming tile marked with spots or pips
a loose cloak with a hood worn at masquerades

explanation.surface: Something generally seen wearing a cloak with a hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as seen, but means marked with dots like a gaming tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaming tile is marked with pips; the word also names a masquerade cloak with a hood.

clue.text: Interrupt the speaker — to hell with the French!

parts.note: heck is a mild substitute for hell
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone shouts down a speaker, cursing the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack a public speaker with jeers is to interrupt them.

clue.text: For a Roman she was unusually puritanical, lacking sex appeal

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of puritanical are rearranged, with some left over

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A Roman woman was strangely strait-laced and not at all alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' says IT is removed: PURITANICAL rearranged, less I and T, gives the answer. Calpurnia was the wife of Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Calpurnia was the third wife of Julius Caesar, a noblewoman of ancient Rome.

clue.text: An angel, this unmarried girl

indicators.note: un-married means the letter M, for married, is taken away

parts.note: Muriel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone praises a single young woman as heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the standard abbreviation for married; removing it from MURIEL leaves the archangel.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriel is one of the archangels in Jewish and Christian tradition.

clue.text: Dissolute, but not tight

explanation.surface: Someone debauched but, surprisingly, sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not tight' could mean sober, tight being slang for drunk, but it means slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Of morals, lax and wanton; of a fastening, slack and free.

clue.text: Parts of the piste without the right sparkle

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters go round the letter for right
the word piste is split into parts and rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Sections of a ski run lack the right glitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts of' makes ESPIT from PISTE; 'without' puts that round R, giving ESP-R-IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit, a sparkle of spirit in conversation.

clue.text: The top's come off this pinta

definitions.text: The top's come off this pinta

parts.words: The top's come off this pinta
parts.note: the top is the cream layer that rises on a bottle of milk; pinta is British slang for a pint of milk

explanation.surface: Someone notices the cap is missing from the milk bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, once delivered to doorsteps in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk from which the cream has been removed is the low-fat kind.

clue.text: Nuts on fruit for breakfast?

parts.note: describes a Swiss morning cereal of oats with nuts and dried fruit, though it reads like a craze for fruit

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with having fruit at the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts on' looks like 'crazy about', but the nuts are literal ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss breakfast cereal of rolled oats mixed with nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Cave explorer needs room to turn round for a start

indicators.note: for a start means these letters come at the front, before the word for room
turn says the little word to is flipped end to end

parts.note: taken as written
a round shape stands for the letter O
room means scope, space to operate

explanation.surface: A potholer needs space to manoeuvre when setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is a body cavity, the ear: the instrument a doctor uses to examine it is the 'explorer'. 'turn' makes OT from TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical instrument for examining the ear canal probes a hollow in the body.
